name: Ahom period
summary: The Tai-Ahom kingdom of Upper (Ujoni) Assam, founded by Sukaphaa in 1228 and ended by the Burmese invasions and the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826: its kings, queens, nobles and rebels, and the foreign commanders they fought.
group_order: Ahom kings; Ahom queens and royal family; Ahom officers and generals; Moamoria rebels; Mughal and Bengal commanders; Burmese and British figures

name: Chaolung Sukaphaa
summary: Born around 1189 in Mong Mao, he left in 1215, crossed the Patkai hills and reached Namrup in December 1228, founding the Ahom kingdom that lasted until 1826. He built Charaideo in 1253.
notes: Married daughters of the Moran chief Badaucha and the Barahi chief Thakumatha. Moved his base from 1236 (Mungklang) through Habung (1240) and Ligirigaon (1244) before Charaideo.

summary: Descending into Namrup, Sukaphaa establishes firm frontier peace through tactical deterrence and diplomatic accords with eastern Naga chieftains.

summary: Sukaphaa and scouts view the immense, fertile Brahmaputra River plain ('Mung Dun Sun Kham' - Country of Golden Gardens), recognizing its potential for wet-rice cultivation.

name: Sukaphaa Enters the Assam Valley
summary: Formal arrival of Sukaphaa's royal entourage in the plains of Upper Assam along the Dihing river basin in 1228 CE, officially inaugurating the 600-year Ahom Dynasty.
notes: Arrival at Namrup in December 1228. In the same year Sandhya took the throne of Kamarupa.

name: Establishment of the First Tai Settlements
summary: Initial settlements established at Tipam, Habung, and Shimolguri; stilt houses (Rwan-hon) constructed and virgin floodplains cleared for agriculture.

name: The Sacred Promontory of Charaideo
summary: The sacred royal compound and ancestral temples at Charaideo, the spiritual center and eternal resting place of Ahom royalty.

name: Institution of the Supreme Offices of Burhagohain and Borgohain
summary: Sukaphaa institutes the Great Council of Nobles: Thaomung Klinglunmang (Burhagohain) and Thaomung Kangngan (Borgohain), forming a hereditary prime-ministerial council.

name: Matrimonial Alliances with Borahi and Moran Rulers
summary: Sukaphaa adopts an assimilative policy by establishing matrimonial bonds with the indigenous Moran chief Bodousa and the Borahi king Thakumtha, marrying local princesses and integrating them into court governance.

name: Introduction of Advanced Wet-Rice Cultivation (Sali Kheti)
summary: Introduction of advanced Tai hydraulic techniques, dyke bunding, canal irrigation, and deep-water transplanted Sali rice, producing an agricultural surplus.

name: Founding and Construction of the Sacred Capital at Charaideo
summary: In 1253 CE, Sukaphaa establishes the permanent royal capital at Charaideo (Che-Rai-Doi), consecrated with sacred Tai Phuralong rituals and ancestral invocations.

name: Writing of the First Ahom Buranji (Royal Chronicles)
summary: Sukaphaa decrees that royal scribes and priests record every event, battle, decree, and genealogy on Sanchi bark (agarwood paper), establishing Assam's Buranji tradition.

name: The Royal Court of Sukaphaa
summary: Convening of the sovereign assembly at Charaideo; state administration organized with local leaders integrated, establishing a harmonious multi-ethnic polity.

name: Institution of Royal Moidams (Pyramidal Earth Tumuli)
summary: Upon Sukaphaa's demise in 1268 CE, the tradition of building subterranean vaulted brick/stone chambers covered by hemispherical earthen mounds (Moidams) begins at Charaideo.

name: Accession and Court Assembly of Suteuphaa
summary: Sukaphaa's eldest son assumes the golden throne and addresses the council of ministers to set aggressive policies for western border expansion.

name: Frontier Standoff on the Dikhou River
summary: Ahom expanding settlements encounter the Kachari Kingdom's eastern outpost along the Dikhou River.

name: Skirmishes on the Ahom-Kachari Frontier
summary: Military clashes between Ahom warriors and Kachari troops over control of fertile grazing and cultivation tracts along the Dikhou.

name: Diplomatic Negotiations with the Kachari King
summary: Suteuphaa sends envoys to avoid destructive protracted war, initiating bilateral talks with the Kachari monarch.

name: Demarcation of the Dikhou River Boundary
summary: Formal treaty demarcating the Dikhou River as the permanent mutual frontier between the Ahoms and Kacharis.

name: Conspiracy of the Eastern Naga Clans
summary: Highland Naga chieftains withhold promised tributes and plot coordinated raids on Ahom valley villages.

name: Suteuphaa Marshals the Royal Army
summary: King Suteuphaa mobilizes an expeditionary army equipped with iron-tipped arrows, daos, and war shields into the foothills.

name: The Fierce Battle of the Naga Hills
summary: Ahom forces fight intense uphill engagements against fortified Naga hill positions, defeating hostile warriors in dense jungle terrain.

name: Naga Submission and Tribute Offering
summary: Defeated Naga chiefs travel to the royal court at Charaideo to kneel, submit oaths of loyalty, and pay tribute in salt, iron, and cloths.

name: Consolidation of the Dikhou Frontier
summary: Peaceful agrarian settlements flourish across the pacified Dikhou frontier, securing Upper Assam's borders.

name: Administrative Division of the Realm
summary: Subinphaa formally partitions administrative jurisdiction and subjects into two equal domains under the Burhagohain and Borgohain.

name: Dual Provincial Governance by Gohains
summary: Burhagohain administers the northern/eastern territory while Borgohain administers the southern/western territory with autonomous judicial authority.

name: Large-scale Swamp Reclamation and Bunding
summary: Large-scale drainage canals, dykes, and earthen bunds constructed across alluvial marshlands to open vast new paddy fields.

name: Outbreak of the First Ahom-Kamata War
summary: King Sukhangphaa leads an offensive against Raja Durlabhanarayana of Kamata, seeking westward expansion into Lower Assam.

name: Military Stalemate in the Kamata Campaign
summary: After prolonged fighting and sieges without either side securing a decisive victory, both monarchs recognize mutual exhaustion.

name: Ahom-Kamata Royal Matrimonial Treaty
summary: Peace concluded by the marriage of Kamata Princess Rajani (Durlabhanarayana's daughter) to Sukhangphaa, sealing durable inter-kingdom peace.
notes: Wikipedia (Sukhaangphaa) dates the end of the war to 1324, against c. 1308 here; it names both princesses, Rajani and Bhajani.

name: Birth of Prince Chao Pulai
summary: Princess Rajani gives birth to Prince Chao Pulai, tying the royal lineages of Kamata and Ahom together.

name: Chao Pulai's Revolt and Alliance with Kamata
summary: Chao Pulai disputes the succession of his half-brother Sukhrangphaa and conspires with maternal Kamata envoys for military support.

name: Fraternal Reconciliation Between Sukhrangphaa and Chao Pulai
summary: Rather than shedding fraternal blood, Sukhrangphaa welcomes Chao Pulai back into the court and effects complete reconciliation.

name: Appointment of Chao Pulai as Governor of Sadiya
summary: King Sukhrangphaa invests Chao Pulai with governorship of the critical eastern frontier outpost of Sadiya.

name: Safrai River Diplomatic Peace Summit
summary: King Sutuphaa meets the Chutia monarch on the Safrai river for joint festivities and peace negotiations to resolve frontier friction.

name: Betrayal and Assassination of King Sutuphaa
summary: During a boat excursion on the Safrai river, the Chutia king treacherously assassinates Sutuphaa aboard the barge, triggering centuries of bitter warfare.

name: First Ministerial Interregnum
summary: Following Sutuphaa's treacherous assassination, the Burhagohain and Borgohain rule jointly for four years due to the absence of an acceptable adult royal prince.
notes: Wikipedia counts three interregnums (1364–1369, 1376–1380, 1389–1397), so this is the second.

name: Banishment of the Pregnant Younger Queen
summary: While King Tyao Khamti is away battling Chutias, his jealous Chief Queen falsely accuses the beloved younger queen and sentences her to be cast adrift on a raft down the Brahmaputra.

name: Birth of Prince Sudang in Habung Village
summary: The banished pregnant queen washes ashore at Habung and is sheltered by a pious Brahmin family; she gives birth to prince Sudang before passing away.

name: Assassination of King Tyao Khamti
summary: Disgusted by Tyao Khamti's acquiescence in the murder of his innocent queen and arbitrary rule, nobles and citizens revolt and assassinate the king.

name: Second Ministerial Interregnum
summary: Ministers Burhagohain and Borgohain hold executive power for eight years following the assassination of Tyao Khamti while searching for the exiled royal prince.
notes: Wikipedia counts three interregnums (1364–1369, 1376–1380, 1389–1397), so this is the third.

name: Prince Sudang Raised in Brahmin Household
summary: Prince Sudang grows up oblivious to his royal identity, tending cattle and studying Sanskrit scriptures alongside Brahmin children at Habung.

name: Sudangphaa Identity Confirmation
summary: Official confirmation of royal bloodline presented to Prince Sudang at Habung by council messengers.

name: Ministers Discover the Hidden Prince Sudang at Habung
summary: After eight years of search, the Burhagohain's emissaries locate the rightful heir Prince Sudang living as an ordinary cowherd at Habung.
notes: Thao Cheoken found the prince; the Burhagohain brought him to Charaideo.

name: Triumphant Royal Return of Sudang to Charaideo
summary: Prince Sudang is escorted in state barge flotillas up the Brahmaputra to Charaideo accompanied by his Brahmin foster-family.

name: Coronation of Sudangphaa
summary: Grand accession ceremony where Prince Sudang ascends the throne taking the Tai title Chao Siu-Dang-Pha.

name: The Reign of Bamuni Konwar
summary: Sudangphaa rewards his Brahmin foster father and brothers with high court offices, inaugurating Hindu Brahminical influence.

name: Institution of the Singari-Gharutha Coronation
summary: Sudangphaa inaugurates the sacred Singari-gharutha ceremony, ascending a raised platform of Singari timber, washing in sacred waters, and killing a bull/buffalo.

name: Harmonious Synthesis of Tai and Hindu Vedic Rituals
summary: Court ceremonies conduct Vedic homa rituals alongside traditional Tai worship of Somdeo and Me-Dam-Me-Phi ancestor rites.

name: Harmonious Synthesis of Tai and Hindu Vedic Rituals
summary: Court ceremonies conduct Vedic homa rituals alongside traditional Tai worship of Somdeo and Me-Dam-Me-Phi ancestor rites.

name: Matrimonial Alliance with Bhuyan Chieftains
summary: Sudangphaa secures stability across the north bank by establishing marriage ties with powerful Baro-Bhuyan chieftains.

name: Administrative Centralization at Charagua
summary: Constructs the new capital city Charagua on the Dihing river to better oversee burgeoning agricultural lands and trade routes.

name: Cultural Renaissance and Literary Patronage
summary: Sudangphaa patronizes both Tai chroniclers and Sanskrit scholars, fostering bilingualism and literary learning in court.

name: Peaceful Reign of Sujanphaa
summary: Sujanphaa preserves external peace and internal order across Upper Assam for fifteen unbroken years.

name: Consolidation Under Suphakphaa
summary: Son of Sujanphaa; a steady seventeen-year reign promoting trade, agricultural stability, and peace with neighboring hill tribes.

name: The Golden Forty-Nine-Year Peace of Susenphaa
summary: One of the longest reigns in Ahom annals; nearly five decades of uninterrupted agricultural and population growth.

name: Tangshu Naga Raids on Lowland Settlements
summary: Tangshu Naga warriors raid eastern border villages, looting grain stores and capturing lowland subjects.

name: Susenphaa's Punitive Tangshu Campaign
summary: Susenphaa personally leads an army into the rugged Tangshu hills, encircling rebel villages and cutting off mountain passes.

name: Submission and Tribute of the Tangshu Chiefs
summary: Defeated Tangshu leaders present offerings of swords, amber, and mountain goods, swearing eternal peace with the Ahom throne.

name: Erection of Charaideo Boundary Stones
summary: Inscribed stone monoliths erected around the holy hills of Charaideo to permanently safeguard the royal necropolis.

name: The Battle of Turung Against the Kacharis
summary: Ahom forces clash fiercely with Kachari armies near the Dikhou; Ahom army suffers a tactical reverse leading to temporary tribute concessions.

name: Peace Settlement with the Kacharis
summary: Suhenphaa concludes peace with the Kachari king through tribute of royal princesses and elephants, stabilizing the southern flank.

name: Tangshu Ambush of Borgohain Khenphung
summary: During a patrol in the eastern hill tracts, Borgohain Khenphung is ambushed by hostile Tangshu warriors but manages a fighting retreat.

name: Suhenphaa's Inspection of Palace Works
summary: King Suhenphaa walks unescorted among workmen to inspect new wooden palace structures at Charagua.

name: Assassination of King Suhenphaa
summary: Turung palace laborers conceal weapons and spear King Suhenphaa to death inside the palace under cover of darkness.

name: Assassination of King Suhenphaa
summary: Turung palace laborers conceal weapons and spear King Suhenphaa to death inside the palace under cover of darkness.

name: Royal Inquest and Execution of Suhenphaa's Assassins
summary: Supimphaa convenes a tribunal, identifies the conspirators behind his father's murder, and executes them publicly.

name: Supimphaa Exiles Pregnant Queen to the Nagas
summary: Due to malicious palace gossip, Supimphaa banishes his pregnant queen to the village of a loyal Naga chief.

name: Birth of Konseng in the Naga Foothills
summary: The exiled queen gives birth to prince Konseng among the Nagas, raised in mountain traditions before returning to court.

name: Konseng's Return and Presentation to King Suhungmung
summary: Grown into a stalwart warrior, Konseng is brought from the Naga village to Bakata; Suhungmung acknowledges him as half-brother of royal blood.

name: Creation of the Office of Barpatragohain
summary: Suhungmung creates a third great ministerial post—the Barpatragohain—elevating Konseng to equal rank with Burhagohain and Borgohain.

name: Adoption of the Title Swarganarayan and Saka Calendar
summary: Suhungmung officially assumes the Sanskrit title 'Swarganarayan' (Lord of Heaven), introducing the Saka calendar into state epigraphy.

name: Ahom Vanguard Marches Against the Chutia Kingdom
summary: Suhungmung marches an immense land and naval force up the Brahmaputra to confront Chutia monarch Dhirnarayan.

name: Annexation of the Chutia Kingdom
summary: Chutia forces routed at Chandangiri; Sadiya annexed into the Ahom Empire; office of Sadiya-Khowa Gohain instituted; firearms and copper-plate treasures acquired.
notes: Habung was taken in 1512 and Dhirnarayan routed at Dibru in 1523; by 1524 Phrasengmung Borgohain governed Sadiya.

name: Konseng Fortifies the Western Border
summary: Konseng Barpatragohain deploys stockades, signal towers, and cannon batteries along the western border to counter Bengal Sultanate raids.

name: Repulse of Early Bengal Sultanate Invasions
summary: Ahom armies defeat Bengal Sultanate commanders Bit Malik and Mit Manik in naval battles, capturing artillery and cavalry horses.

name: The Great Invasion of Commander Turbak
summary: General Turbak invades Assam with a large Gaur army armed with muskets, heavy cannons, and cavalry.

name: Decisive Victory Over Turbak and Pursuit to Karatoya
summary: Konseng Barpatragohain slays Turbak on the battlefield; Bengal forces routed; Ahoms pursue retreating invaders to the sacred Karatoya River.

name: Accession of Suklenmung
summary: Suklenmung ascends the throne following Suhungmung's death, establishing Garhgaon as the royal residence.

name: Construction of Fortified Capital Garhgaon and Naga Ali
summary: Excavates the monumental Garhgaon moat and earthen ramparts, builds brick gateways, and constructs the great Naga Ali military road.

name: Battle of Pichala Against Koch Forces
summary: Suklenmung defends his kingdom against invading Koch commander Chilarai along the Pichala River, repulsing Koch forces with heavy losses.

name: Solemn Celebration of the Rikkhvan Ceremony
summary: Performance of the ancient Tai Rikkhvan ritual to restore royal vitality, longevity, and invincibility in battle.

name: Royal Procession of King Sukhaamphaa
summary: Magnificent procession of Sukhaamphaa riding atop the royal tusker through Garhgaon with gold-embroidered silk standards.

name: Royal Procession of King Sukhaamphaa
summary: Magnificent procession of Sukhaamphaa riding atop the royal tusker through Garhgaon with gold-embroidered silk standards.

name: Chilarai's Invasion of Garhgaon
summary: Koch king Naranarayan and general Chilarai launch a blitzkrieg; Ahoms execute a tactical retreat into the hills of Namrup.

name: The Treaty of Majuli
summary: Peace treaty negotiated on Majuli island; Ahoms cede north bank lands and send royal hostages, enabling subsequent reclamation after Koch departure.

name: The Long Peace and Cultural Growth Under Khora Raja
summary: Following early wars, Sukhaamphaa's kingdom experiences prolonged domestic peace, flourishing commerce, and arts.

name: Accession of Susenghphaa (Pratap Singha)
summary: Pratap Singha ascends the throne at Garhgaon, inaugurating decades of revolutionary governance and resistance against the Mughal Empire.

name: Accession of Susenghphaa (Pratap Singha)
summary: Pratap Singha ascends the throne at Garhgaon, inaugurating decades of revolutionary governance and resistance against the Mughal Empire.

name: Reorganization of the Paik System by Momai Tamuli Barbarua
summary: Momai Tamuli reorganizes adult males into Paik squads (Gots of 3 or 4 men), mandatory rotation of state labor, and khel guilds, transforming Assam's agrarian and military mobilization.

name: Institution of the Offices of Borbarua and Borphukan
summary: Pratap Singha creates two supreme executive posts: the Borbarua (prime administrator & chief judicial magistrate) and Borphukan (viceroy & supreme military warden of Lower Assam).

name: Treaty of Asurar Ali and Western Defense Line
summary: Following repeated repulses of Mughal invasions, Pratap Singha signs the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639) with Allah Yar Khan, formalizing the Barnadi River as the frontier.

name: Tyranny and Court Intrigue Under Suramphaa
summary: Suramphaa becomes infatuated with a concubine, disregarding ministers and executing loyal nobles arbitrarily.

name: Deposition and Poisoning of Suramphaa
summary: The council of ministers deposes the tyrannical king and removes him from power.

name: The Frail Reign of Sutingphaa
summary: Afflicted by chronic disease and goitre, Sutingphaa struggles to rule while court factions vie for supremacy.

name: Prince Sutamla Organizes Court Loyalists
summary: Prince Sutamla rallies ministers and soldiers to remove his incapacitated father to restore imperial governance.

name: Coronation of Jayadhwaj Singha
summary: Sutamla ascends the throne taking the regal Hindu name Jayadhwaj Singha, the first Ahom monarch to issue coins with Sanskrit inscriptions.

name: Adoption of Hindu Rituals in Sutamla's Court
summary: Sutamla formalizes Hindu court rituals, patronizing Vaishnava monasteries and adopting Sanskrit titulature alongside Tai liturgy.

name: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma
summary: Jayadhwaj takes spiritual initiation from Niranjan Bapu of Auniati Satra, formally adopting Mahapuruxiya Ekasarana Dharma as royal faith.

name: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma
summary: Jayadhwaj takes spiritual initiation from Niranjan Bapu of Auniati Satra, formally adopting Mahapuruxiya Ekasarana Dharma as royal faith.

name: Royal Naam-Prasanga and Satra Endowments
summary: The king participates in choral chanting (Naam-Prasanga) and donates extensive rent-free lands and paiks to the satras of Majuli.

name: Mir Jumla's Imperial Mughal Invasion
summary: Aurangzeb's premier general and Viceroy of Bengal, Mir Jumla, advances up the Brahmaputra with 12,000 cavalry, 30,000 infantry, and 323 armed war boats.

name: Mughal Capture of Capital Garhgaon
summary: Mir Jumla enters Garhgaon in victory; thousands of Ahom cannons, gold treasures, and grain reserves are captured by imperial Mughal forces.

name: The Monsoon Counter-War of Namrup
summary: From hills of Namrup, Jayadhwaj unleashes guerrilla warfare during torrential monsoons, severing Mughal supply lines and decimating Mir Jumla's trapped army with epidemic fever.

name: The Treaty of Ghilajharighat
summary: Severely ill Mir Jumla and exhausted Jayadhwaj sign treaty; Ahoms cede Western Assam, pay war indemnities of gold, silver, 90 elephants, and send princesses.

name: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
summary: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

name: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
summary: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

name: King Jayadhwaj Singha's Vow of Liberation
summary: Brokenhearted by the humiliating treaty and daughter's departure, Jayadhwaj returns to ruined Garhgaon and urges the court never to rest until the Mughals are expelled.

name: Deathbed of King Jayadhwaj Singha
summary: On his deathbed at Bakata, Jayadhwaj extracts a solemn oath from his successor Chakradhwaj Singha to wipe out the shame of Mughal conquest.

name: Chakradhwaj Singha's Oath of Resistance
summary: Receiving a patronizing Mughal royal robe (khilat) from Delhi, King Chakradhwaj angrily throws it down, proclaiming: 'Death is preferable to a state of subordination to the Bengas!'

name: Lachit Tested and Appointed Supreme Commander
summary: Chakradhwaj tests Lachit's presence of mind with a staged court insult; impressed by his fierce dignity, the king confers the golden sword and supreme command of the army to liberate Guwahati.

name: Lachit Borphukan Liberates Guwahati
summary: Ahom forces execute a coordinated amphibious night assault, breaching the Mughal ramparts and driving imperial troops out of Guwahati.

name: Lachit Borphukan Liberates Guwahati
summary: Ahom forces execute a coordinated amphibious night assault, breaching the Mughal ramparts and driving imperial troops out of Guwahati.

name: Recapture of the Strategic Fort of Itakhuli
summary: Lachit storm-attacks the strategic Itakhuli fortress, capturing vast Mughal artillery, war sloops, and driving imperial forces beyond the Manas.

name: The Tragic Battle of Alaboi
summary: Compelled by Chakradhwaj to engage Ram Singh's cavalry on open plains, 10,000 Ahom braves perish in a single day; Lachit weeps bitterly for his fallen soldiers.

name: Total Military Reorganization After Alaboi
summary: Chakradhwaj and Lachit regroup, constructing massive defensive mud ramparts (Gars) around Saraighat and converting strategy to pure riverine warfare.

name: Total Military Reorganization After Alaboi
summary: Chakradhwaj and Lachit regroup, constructing massive defensive mud ramparts (Gars) around Saraighat and converting strategy to pure riverine warfare.

name: War Council of Udayaditya Singha and Lachit Borphukan
summary: Upon succeeding Chakradhwaj, Udayaditya reaffirms complete faith in Lachit Borphukan, coordinating logistics for the impending Mughal clash.

name: War Council of Udayaditya Singha and Lachit Borphukan
summary: Upon succeeding Chakradhwaj, Udayaditya reaffirms complete faith in Lachit Borphukan, coordinating logistics for the impending Mughal clash.

name: Fortification of Saraighat and Execution of the Negligent Uncle
summary: Lachit oversees construction of the Saraighat earthen rampart overnight; finding his maternal uncle negligent, he beheads him uttering: 'My uncle is not greater than my country!'

name: Fortification of Saraighat and Execution of the Negligent Uncle
summary: Lachit oversees construction of the Saraighat earthen rampart overnight; finding his maternal uncle negligent, he beheads him uttering: 'My uncle is not greater than my country!'

name: Lachit Rallies Retreating Troops from His Sickbed
summary: Suffering from severe high fever, Lachit orders his sickbed carried onto his royal war-boat, shouting to retreating soldiers: 'If you wish to flee, do so! But let the King know I died fighting!'

name: The Epic Naval Battle of Saraighat
summary: Ahom fleet traps Ram Singh's Mughal armada at the narrowest gorge of the Brahmaputra at Saraighat; Mughal naval force is completely shattered in a historic tactical masterpiece.

name: The Epic Naval Battle of Saraighat
summary: Ahom fleet traps Ram Singh's Mughal armada at the narrowest gorge of the Brahmaputra at Saraighat; Mughal naval force is completely shattered in a historic tactical masterpiece.

name: The Expedition Against the Daflas
summary: Expedition launched to pacify Dafla hillmen raiding north bank villages; harsh conditions test the royal army.

name: Portrait of Lachit Borphukan
summary: Regal portrait of the legendary Ahom generalissimo Lachit Borphukan, victor of the epic Battle of Saraighat.

name: Portrait of Lachit Borphukan
summary: Regal portrait of the legendary Ahom generalissimo Lachit Borphukan, victor of the epic Battle of Saraighat.

name: Rise of Debera Borbarua's Palace Reign of Terror
summary: Debera Borbarua accumulates absolute despotic control, executing rival ministers, princes, and courtiers with impunity.

name: Rise of Debera Borbarua's Palace Reign of Terror
summary: Debera Borbarua accumulates absolute despotic control, executing rival ministers, princes, and courtiers with impunity.

name: Debera Borbarua Installs and Murders the Samaguria Raja
summary: Debera poisons Ramdhwaj and installs Suhung as puppet monarch; when Suhung questions his authority, Debera assassinates him in 20 days.

name: Gobar Raja Crowned as Debera's Puppet
summary: Debera crowns Tungkhungia prince Gobar (father of Gadadhar Singha) as king to maintain his puppet grip over the throne.

name: Atan Burhagohain Captures Garhgaon and Executes Debera and Gobar
summary: Atan Burhagohain leads an army of loyalist commanders from Guwahati to Garhgaon, arrests and executes Debera and deposes Gobar.

name: Installation of Sujinphaa by Atan Burhagohain
summary: Noble statesman Atan Burhagohain refuses the crown himself and adheres strictly to constitution by placing Dihingia prince Sujinphaa on the throne.

name: Court Suspicion and Rift Between King and Premier
summary: Influenced by plotting sons and courtiers, Sujinphaa begins to view the immensely popular Atan Burhagohain with bitter suspicion.

name: The Royal Army Deserts Sujinphaa
summary: When Sujinphaa attempts an armed ambush against the Burhagohain, royal soldiers refuse to strike their beloved prime minister and desert the king.

name: Deposition and Tragic End of Sujinphaa
summary: Sujinphaa is captured, blinded according to Ahom dynastic custom, and passes away in confinement.

name: Accession and Court of Sudoiphaa Paratiya Raja
summary: Paratiya prince ascends the throne; kingdom faces external intrigue from Lower Assam viceroy Laluk Sola Borphukan.

name: Treason of Laluk Sola: Surrender of Guwahati to the Mughals
summary: In an act of monstrous betrayal, Laluk Sola Borphukan surrenders Guwahati to Mughal Prince Azam Tara for 400,000 rupees and promises of being made Raja.

name: Prince Gadapani Escapes into the Hills in Disguise
summary: Forewarned by his courageous wife Joymoti, tall and muscular Prince Gadapani flees in disguise into the Naga hills to evade royal executioners.

name: Installation of the Teenaged Boy-King Sulikphaa
summary: Laluk Sola murders Atan Burhagohain and crowns 14-year-old Sulikphaa (Lora Raja) to govern through terror and usurp power.

name: The Great Purge and Mutilation of Royal Princes
summary: Laluk Sola and Sulikphaa unleash death squads across Assam to kill, blind, or slit the ears of all eligible Ahom princes to disqualify them from the throne.

name: Martyrdom of Princess Joymoti Konwari
summary: Tied to thorn bushes on Jerenga Pathar and brutally tortured for 14 continuous days by Lora Raja's agents, Princess Joymoti breathes her last refusing to betray her husband Gadapani.

name: Gadadhar Singha Takes the Throne and Marshals the Army
summary: Overthrowing Lora Raja, Gadadhar Singha mobilizes the kingdom's armed forces to permanently purge Assam of Mughal occupation.

name: Imperial Conference with Vaishnava Satradhikars
summary: King Gadadhar Singha meets with powerful abbots (Satradhikars), asserting absolute royal authority over monastic wealth and exempt paiks.

name: Royal Visitation to the Satra Naamghar
summary: The austere Swargadeo visits a monastic prayer hall (Naamghar) to ensure monastic orders do not undermine state military recruitment.

name: Coronation of Rudra Singha (Sukhrungphaa)
summary: Son of Joymoti and Gadadhar Singha ascends the throne; initiates the zenith of Ahom political grandeur, architecture, and international diplomacy.

name: Coronation of Rudra Singha (Sukhrungphaa)
summary: Son of Joymoti and Gadadhar Singha ascends the throne; initiates the zenith of Ahom political grandeur, architecture, and international diplomacy.

name: Founding and Construction of Capital City Rangpur and Joysagar
summary: Constructs the glorious capital Rangpur ('City of Joy'), excavates the massive Joysagar tank in memory of mother Joymoti, and builds Namdang stone bridge.

name: Founding and Construction of Capital City Rangpur and Joysagar
summary: Constructs the glorious capital Rangpur ('City of Joy'), excavates the massive Joysagar tank in memory of mother Joymoti, and builds Namdang stone bridge.

name: King Rudra Singha Inaugurates Royal Festivities at Rang Ghar
summary: Rudra Singha presides over Rongali Bihu festivities, buffalo fights, elephant encounters, and folk dances from the royal pavilion at Rang Ghar.

name: King Rudra Singha Inaugurates Royal Festivities at Rang Ghar
summary: Rudra Singha presides over Rongali Bihu festivities, buffalo fights, elephant encounters, and folk dances from the royal pavilion at Rang Ghar.

name: Subjugation and Vassalage of the Kachari and Jaintia Rulers
summary: Following victorious campaigns, Rudra Singha receives envoys and rulers of the Kacharis and Jaintias who submit tribute and acknowledge Ahom supremacy.

name: Grand Durbar and the Seven-Tiered Singhason at Rangpur
summary: Rudra Singha presides from the legendary jewel-inlaid lion throne (Singhason) under a golden canopy, welcoming foreign envoys from all corners of India.

name: Grand Durbar and the Seven-Tiered Singhason at Rangpur
summary: Rudra Singha presides from the legendary jewel-inlaid lion throne (Singhason) under a golden canopy, welcoming foreign envoys from all corners of India.

name: Grand Durbar and the Seven-Tiered Singhason at Rangpur
summary: Rudra Singha presides from the legendary jewel-inlaid lion throne (Singhason) under a golden canopy, welcoming foreign envoys from all corners of India.

name: Transfer of Royal Power to Queen Phuleswari (Bar Raja)
summary: Panicked by astrological predictions of Chhatra-bhanga (loss of kingship), Siva Singha transfers the sovereign umbrella, royal seal, and rule to his chief queen Phuleswari.

name: Excavation of Gaurisagar Tank and Temples
summary: Queen Phuleswari excavates Gaurisagar tank and erects temples dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Devi along its banks.

name: Queen Phuleswari's Persecution of Moamoria Vaishnavas
summary: Queen Phuleswari aggressively enforces Shakta worship, compelling Moamoria Vaishnavite Mahantas to smear sacrificial animal blood on their foreheads, igniting decades of bitter hatred.

name: Construction of Sivasagar Tank (Bor Pukhuri) and Shiva Dol
summary: Queen Ambika excavates the monumental 257-acre Sivasagar tank and erects the 104-foot-high Shiva Dol, one of India's tallest stone temple shikhara towers.

name: The Great Cadastral Land Survey (Pek-Kakar)
summary: Comprehensive statewide land measurement and census of households and cultivation acreage conducted across Assam.

name: Construction and Dedication of the Masonry Rang Ghar
summary: Pramatta Singha reconstructs Rang Ghar in permanent fired brick and egg-mortar as a magnificent two-storied oval sports colosseum.

name: Royal Buffalo Fights on Rupahi Pathar
summary: The King and royal court watch thrilling buffalo fights, bird duels, and martial acrobatics held in the arena beneath the pavilion arches.

name: Royal Court Assembly at the Rang Ghar Pavilion
summary: Aristocratic gathering of Gohains, royal ladies, and vassal chiefs on the terrace of Rang Ghar during spring festivities.

name: Expansion of the Grand Talatal Ghar Palace
summary: Rajeswar Singha expands Talatal Ghar into a 7-storied architectural wonder (4 above ground, 3 underground) equipped with secret evacuation tunnels to Dikhou river.

name: Lata-Katai Ran: The Mountain Expedition to Manipur
summary: Rajeswar Singha dispatches an army across trackless, creepers-choked mountain jungles ('Lata-Katai Ran') to liberate Manipur from Burmese occupation and reinstate Meitei King Jai Singh.

name: Royal Wedding of Rajeswar Singha and Princess Kuranganayani
summary: In gratitude, King Jai Singh gives his heroic daughter Princess Kuranganayani in marriage to Rajeswar Singha, cementing eternal Ahom-Manipuri ties.

name: Outbreak of the First Moamoria Rebellion
summary: Enraged by insults to their Guru, peasant masses and Moran disciples of the Moamoria Satra revolt, routing royal forces and capturing the capital Rangpur.

name: Captivity and Imprisonment of King Lakshmi Singha
summary: Rebels capture Swargadeo Lakshmi Singha, imprison him at the Joysagar temple, and declare Ramakanta as ruler and Ragha Moran as Barbarua.

name: Queen Kuranganayani's Daring Counter-Coup
summary: During Rongali Bihu, Queen Kuranganayani bravely strikes down the usurper Ragha Moran with a sword blow from behind; loyalist nobles storm the palace and liberate King Lakshmi Singha.

name: Royal Retribution and Repression of Moamoria Rebels
summary: Restored royal government executes thousands of Moamoria adherents and leaders, cementing irreversible societal rifts.

name: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

name: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

name: Flight of King Gaurinath Singha Down the Brahmaputra
summary: Swargadeo Gaurinath flees in despair from burning Upper Assam on royal barges to take refuge in Guwahati.

name: British Military Intervention: Captain Thomas Welsh Expedition
summary: Responding to Gaurinath's appeal, British East India Company sends 6 companies of sepoys under Captain Thomas Welsh who defeat rebels and re-enter Rangpur.

name: The Ahom-British Commercial Treaty of 1793
summary: First formal commercial agreement signed between Ahom monarchy and the British East India Company, regulating customs and trade between Bengal and Assam.

name: The Autocratic Regency of Premier Purnananda Burhagohain
summary: Purnananda Burhagohain exercises de facto sovereign rule, establishing Jorhat as new capital, drilling troops with modern British flintlocks, and suppressing insurrections.

name: Deadly Court Factionalism Between Burhagohain and Borphukan
summary: Young Chandrakanta Singha sides with favorite Satram against the elderly Purnananda; Badan Chandra Borphukan conspires against the premier.

name: The First Burmese Invasion (Manor Din Begins)
summary: Badan Chandra brings a Burmese army of 16,000 soldiers across the Patkai; Purnananda dies of heartbreak; Burmese defeat Ahom troops at Ghiladhari and march on Jorhat.

name: The First Burmese Invasion (Manor Din Begins)
summary: Badan Chandra brings a Burmese army of 16,000 soldiers across the Patkai; Purnananda dies of heartbreak; Burmese defeat Ahom troops at Ghiladhari and march on Jorhat.

name: Assassination of Traitor Badan Chandra Borphukan
summary: Subedar Rup Singh strikes down Badan Chandra Borphukan with a dao while bathing in Jorhat, executing retribution for bringing Burmese invaders.

name: Deposition of Chandrakanta and Accession of Purandar Singha
summary: Ruchinath Burhagohain captures Jorhat, slits Chandrakanta's right ear to permanently disqualify him from kingship, and crowns Purandar Singha.

name: Second Burmese Invasion and Flight of Purandar Singha
summary: Burmese monarch sends large army under Ala Mingi; Purandar and Ruchinath are routed at Nazira and flee into British Bengal territory.

name: Restoration of Chandrakanta Singha as Burmese Puppet
summary: Burmese restore ear-mutilated Chandrakanta to the throne, but Burmese generals retain real power.

name: Chandrakanta's Resistance and Flight from Burmese Reign of Terror
summary: When Burmese attempt to murder him, Chandrakanta flees to British frontier and organizes armed resistance against Burmese pillagers.

name: Burmese Atrocities (Manor Din) Under Puppet Jogeswar Singha
summary: Burmese install powerless puppet Jogeswar Singha while massacring tens of thousands of Assamese civilians, depopulating entire districts.

name: Outbreak of the First Anglo-Burmese War in Assam
summary: British East India Company declares war on Burma; British regiments and gunboats advance up the Brahmaputra, expelling Burmese forces.

name: Expulsion of the Burmese from Upper Assam
summary: Colonel Richards defeats and forces surrender of the Burmese garrison at Rangpur stockade in January 1825.

name: Signing of the Historic Treaty of Yandabo
summary: The King of Ava formally cedes all claims to Assam to the British East India Company, terminating 598 years of independent Ahom rule.

name: Restoration of Purandar Singha as Protected Tributary Ruler
summary: British East India Company reinstates Purandar Singha over Upper Assam conditioned on paying an impossible annual tribute of 50,000 Company rupees.

name: Crushing Tax Demands on War-Devastated Population
summary: Purandar struggles desperately to collect taxes from a depopulated and ruined citizenry to satisfy the exorbitant British tribute demand.

name: Crushing Tax Demands on War-Devastated Population
summary: Purandar struggles desperately to collect taxes from a depopulated and ruined citizenry to satisfy the exorbitant British tribute demand.

name: Final British Annexation of Assam and Deposition of Purandar Singha
summary: Accusing him of default and misgovernment, the British formally depose Purandar Singha, annexing Upper Assam into the British Empire and ending the Ahom dynasty forever.

name: Frontier Battle with Kamata Forces
summary: A pitched riverine engagement between Ahom war flotillas and Kamata defensive troops along the Lower Assam river passes.

name: Frontier Battle with Kamata Forces
summary: A pitched riverine engagement between Ahom war flotillas and Kamata defensive troops along the Lower Assam river passes.

name: Foreign Captives Brought Before the Ahom Golden Throne
summary: Captured enemy generals, cavalry officers, and spoils of war presented before the Swarganarayan in solemn assembly.

name: Ahom Naval Flotilla River Engagement
summary: Ahom Bachari war-boats and rowers maneuver against enemy rivercraft with bowmen and bow mounted swivel-guns.

name: Strategic War Council in the Royal Chamber
summary: The king and top commanders review maps, troop movements, river currents, and fortress fortifications on the eve of battle.

name: The Swarganarayan Invests the Royal Commander
summary: The monarch presents the consecrated Hengdang (royal curved sword) and battle garments to the appointed general.

name: Ahom Commander Kneels in Fealty Before the King
summary: A royal commander kneels before the Ahom throne pledging absolute victory or martyrdom for the homeland.

name: Solemn Vigil at the Royal Deathbed
summary: Court ministers, priests, and queens maintain vigil around the royal bed chamber as a Swargadeo departs for the realm of ancestors.

name: Sudangphaa Repels the Mong Kawng Invasion
summary: The rival claimant Tai Sulai returns with a Mong Kawng (Mungkang) army led by the defector Tasim Pou. Sudangphaa meets it near Kuhiarbari in the Tipam country and defeats it, though he is lightly wounded by a spear.
notes: Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive.

name: Treaty of the Patkai Boundary at Nongnyang Lake
summary: Ahom and Mong Kawng envoys swear a treaty by Nongnyang lake fixing the Patkai range as the border between the two kingdoms. The boundary holds for centuries.
notes: Nongnyang lake as the treaty site follows Gait, A History of Assam; Wikipedia gives only the Patkai boundary. Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive. Painting depicts the two negotiating commanders; Sudangphaa is not physically shown.

name: The Feast Trap for the Tipam Conspirators
summary: Early in his reign the Tipam chiefs plot against the young king. Sudangphaa invites the conspirators to a feast and has them killed.
notes: Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive.

name: Nangchukham Borgohain Marches on Kamata
summary: Tai Sulai flees to Kamata. Sudangphaa's commander Nangchukham Borgohain invades, and the Kamata king, also pressed by Bengal, makes peace and gives a daughter in marriage to Sudangphaa.
notes: Chronology of the Kamata episode is undated and disputed. Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive.

name: Suhungmung Orders the First Count of Fighting Men
summary: Suhungmung orders the first recorded survey of the kingdom's adult men, the base of the later paik militia system.

name: Ahoms Pursue the Kachari King to Dimapur
summary: After five years of war, the Kachari king Khunkhara's army is beaten and its commander killed. The Ahoms chase him to his capital Dimapur; he flees, and Suhungmung installs Detsung as Kachari king.
notes: Khunkhara and Detsung are not yet in the database.

name: Mula Gabharu Falls Fighting Turbak
summary: After her husband Phrasengmung Borgohain is killed by Turbak's army, Princess Mula Gabharu leads women warriors into battle and is killed with five companions. Her death rallies the Ahom army.
notes: Wikipedia names the Battle of Kachua; much of the story (the Kin Lao vow, her speech) is legend.

name: Sack of Dimapur and the End of Detsung
summary: The vassal Kachari king Detsung revolts. The Ahoms pursue him to Jangmarang and kill him; Dimapur is abandoned and the Kacharis move their capital to Maibong. Ahom rule now reaches the Kolong river.
notes: Detsung is not yet in the database.

name: Assassination of Suhungmung
summary: The great king Suhungmung is stabbed in his sleep by his servant Ratiman. His son Suklenmung and a Kachari queen are suspected of the plot.

name: Execution of Hari and Sankardeva Leaves the Ahom Kingdom
summary: Under Suklenmung, Hari, the son-in-law of the Vaishnava saint Sankardeva, is captured and executed. Sankardeva leaves the Ahom kingdom for Koch territory.
notes: Sankardeva and Hari are not yet in the database.

name: Pratap Singha Marries the Koch Princess Mangaldoi
summary: Pratap Singha marries Mangaldoi, daughter of the Koch Hajo king Parikshit Narayan, sealing an alliance against the Mughals.
notes: Wikipedia spells her name Mangaldahi.

name: The Jaintia Bride and the Kachari War
summary: Pratap Singha accepts a Jaintia princess in marriage, but the Kachari king Jasanarayan blocks her passage. War follows; Sundar Gohain drives deep into Kachari land before Bhimbal Konwar's night attack kills him.
notes: Exact year not found; Jasanarayan, Bhimbal Konwar and Sundar Gohain are not yet in the database.

name: Balinarayan Takes Refuge at the Ahom Court
summary: After the Mughals defeat Parikshit of Koch Hajo, his brother Balinarayan flees to Pratap Singha, who makes him tributary raja of Darrang as Dharmanarayan. The refuge angers the Mughal governor Qasim Khan.
notes: Balinarayan is not yet in the database.

name: Night Attack at Samdhara: Abu Bakr's Fleet Destroyed
summary: The first Mughal invasion under Sayyid Abu Bakr and Satrajit takes Kajali, then is destroyed in a night attack by the Bharali–Brahmaputra confluence. Abu Bakr is killed, Satrajit escapes, and Pratap Singha builds a fort at Samdhara inscribed 'Victory in Unequal Battle'.
notes: Wikipedia dates the Battle of Bharali to 1615 and the Battle of Samdhara to January 1616.

name: The Mughal War of 1636–1638
summary: Pratap Singha and Balinarayan push west to Sualkuchi and Hajo. The Mughals under Allah Yar Khan strike back and retake Kamrup; Balinarayan dies, and the Samdhara garrison and the naval fight at Duimunisila stop the Mughal advance.

name: The First Ahom Coins Are Struck
summary: Coins first appear under Jayadhwaj Singha. The old belief that Suklenmung struck the first Ahom coins comes from misread coins of Chakradhwaj Singha.

name: Jayadhwaj Singha Takes Guwahati
summary: While Shah Jahan's sons fight for the Mughal throne, the Mughal faujdar abandons Guwahati. Jayadhwaj Singha's army occupies Kamrup and pushes the Koch king Pran Narayan back beyond Dhubri. This is the direct cause of Mir Jumla's invasion.
notes: Sources disagree whether the Koches or the Ahoms entered Guwahati first.

name: Death of Mir Jumla on the Return March
summary: Sick since the monsoon at Garhgaon, Mir Jumla dies on the way back to Dhaka soon after the Treaty of Ghilajharighat.

name: Death of Lachit Borphukan at Kaliabor
summary: About a year after Saraighat, Lachit Borphukan dies of illness at Kaliabor. Udayaditya Singha builds the Lachit Maidam at Hoolungapara and makes Lachit's brother Laluk Sola the new Borphukan.
notes: Death date given as 25 April 1672 in some sources.

name: Palace Coup Against Udayaditya Singha
summary: Angered by the king's devotion to the ascetic Paramananda Sanyasi and his jailing of Vaishnava mahantas, Debera Hazarika and the king's brother Sarugohain storm the palace at midnight. Udayaditya is taken to Charaideo and killed; his brother takes the throne as Ramdhwaj Singha.
notes: Paramananda Sanyasi is not yet in the database.

name: Murder of Laluk Sola Borphukan
summary: The Borphukan who sold Guwahati to the Mughals is killed by his own bodyguard, ending his hold over the boy-king Sulikphaa.

name: Battle of Itakhuli: The Mughals Driven to the Manas
summary: Gadadhar Singha's three-pronged army and navy close on Guwahati. After the naval battle at Paniduar on 15 August, the Itakhuli fort falls and the Mughals are chased to the Manas river, which becomes the accepted border. The Ahom–Mughal wars end.

name: Gadadhar Singha's Persecution of the Satras
summary: Late in his reign Gadadhar Singha turns on the Vaishnava satras. The Dakhinpat gosain is mutilated and his idols melted down, the Auniati head flees, and Mayamara disciples suffer most. The grievance feeds the later Moamoria rebellion.
notes: Motives (personal grudge or politico-economic) are debated.

name: Rangnath Dol and the Namdang Stone Bridge
summary: Rudra Singha builds the Rangnath Dol and the Namdang stone bridge, cut from a single rock, followed by the Fakuwa Dol in 1703–04.

name: Rudra Singha Plans the Invasion of Bengal
summary: At a general assembly at Rangpur, Rudra Singha announces his plan to invade Mughal Bengal with a league of Hindu rajas, and moves his army to Guwahati.

name: Death of Rudra Singha at the Guwahati Camp
summary: Eight days after falling ill, Rudra Singha dies in camp at Guwahati with the Bengal campaign unlaunched. On his deathbed he tells his son Siva Singha to take Krishnaram Bhattacharya as guru.

name: Krishnaram Bhattacharya Becomes the Parbatiya Gosain
summary: Siva Singha becomes the disciple of the Nabadwip Shakta priest Krishnaram Bhattacharya and gives him charge of the Kamakhya temple on Nilachal hill, where he is known as the Parbatiya Gosain.

name: Painting of the Hastividyarnava
summary: Under Siva Singha and Queen Ambika, Sukumar Barkaith writes the Hastividyarnava, a treatise on royal elephants, illustrated by the painters Dilbar and Dosai.
notes: Sukumar Barkaith, Dilbar and Dosai are not yet in the database.

name: Sarbeswari Becomes the Third Bar Raja
summary: After Ambika's death, Siva Singha raises another queen to rule as Bar Raja under the name Sarbeswari; she holds the title until his death in 1744.
notes: Sources differ on her earlier name (Akari Gabharu or Enadari).

name: Kirti Chandra Borbarua Crowns Rajeswar Singha
summary: On Pramatta Singha's death, the Borbarua Kirti Chandra passes over the elder princes and places Rajeswar Singha on the throne, beginning two decades of his dominance at court.

name: Rebuilding the Kareng Ghar at Garhgaon
summary: Rajeswar Singha replaces the wooden palace at Garhgaon with the brick and stone seven-storey Kareng Ghar that still stands.
notes: The Kareng Ghar infobox gives 1758; the text and the Sivasagar district site give 1752.

name: The Burning of the Buranjis
summary: Stung by the Chakari-pheti Buranji's mockery of his low birth, Kirti Chandra Borbarua has the Buranjis collected and burns those he judges false. Some copies survive.
notes: Most sources place this under Rajeswar Singha; some under Lakshmi Singha. Numali Borgohain (author of the Chakari-pheti) is not yet in the database.

name: The Bihu Ambush on Gaurinath Singha
summary: During Bohag Bihu the Moamorias attack the convoy of the newly crowned Gaurinath Singha. He escapes; the rebels briefly take Rangpur before Ghanashyam Burhagohain retakes it, followed by mass killings.

name: Harihar Tanti's Rising and the Burning of the Majuli Satras
summary: The rebellion resumes from the Dafla hills under Harihar Tanti, joined by Pitambar. Rebels burn the satras of Majuli and march on Rangpur.

name: Bharat Singha Crowned at Rangpur
summary: With Gaurinath in exile at Guwahati, the Moamorias install Bharat Singha as king at Rangpur. He strikes coins claiming descent from Bhagadatta, and is killed in 1799.
notes: Coins in his name are dated 1789–94 and 1796–97.

name: Sarbananda Singha's Capital at Bengmara
summary: The Moamoria leader Sarbananda Singha takes the title Swargadeo and moves his capital from Rangagarah to Bengmara in present-day Tinsukia.

name: The Capital Moves from Rangpur to Jorhat
summary: With Rangpur wrecked by the rebellion, the Ahom court moves its capital to Jorhat, which stays the last capital of the kingdom.
notes: Sources disagree on whether the move was completed before or after Gaurinath's death.

name: Matak Autonomy: Sarbananda Made Barsenapati
summary: After a stalemate at Bengmara, Purnananda Burhagohain recognises Sarbananda as Barsenapati of an autonomous Matak rajya paying annual tribute. The Moamoria rebellion ends.

name: Badan Chandra Borphukan Goes to the Court of Ava
summary: Hunted by Purnananda Burhagohain, Badan Chandra flees to Bengal, is refused help by the East India Company, and reaches the Burmese king Bodawpaya to ask for an army.

name: Chandrakanta Retakes Guwahati
summary: Raising troops in British territory, Chandrakanta Singha recaptures Assam Chowki in October and Guwahati in December 1821.

name: Chandrakanta's Last Stand at Mahgarh
summary: Chandrakanta camps at Mahgarh near Jorhat. Maha Bandula's Burmese army defeats him in April 1822 and he falls back to Guwahati.

name: Defeat at Hadira Chowki; Tilwa Proclaimed Raja of Assam
summary: Mingimaha Tilwa defeats Chandrakanta at Hadira (Assam) Chowki. Chandrakanta withdraws to British territory, and Tilwa is declared Raja of Assam, ending Ahom rule until 1826.
notes: Wikipedia places the defeat in June 1822, with an alternative account in July.

name: Gomdhar Konwar's Revolt
summary: Former Ahom nobles led by Dhananjoy Borgohain crown the prince Gomdhar Konwar near Jorhat and march on Rangpur. Lieutenant Rutherford's troops defeat them; Gomdhar is captured and banished. The first armed rising against British rule in Assam.
notes: Gomdhar Konwar, Dhananjoy Borgohain and Rutherford are not yet in the database.

name: Piyali Phukan and Jiuram Dulia Baruah Hanged
summary: A plot to drive the British out and restore Ahom rule is uncovered. Piyali Phukan, son of Badan Chandra Borphukan, and Jiuram Dulia Baruah are hanged.
notes: Sources differ on the day and place (August or 23 September 1830; Sivasagar or Jorhat) and on Jiuram's name (Dulia Baruah or Medhi). Piyali and Jiuram are not yet in the database; badan-chandra-borphukan is linked only as his father.

name: Interregnum After the Death of Sukhrangphaa
summary: With no acceptable heir after Sukhrangphaa's death, the throne stays empty for five years and the Burhagohain and Borgohain rule. It is the first of three interregnums before 1397.
notes: Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive. Empty royal seat and unnamed ministers; the deceased Sukhrangphaa is not depicted alive.

name: Tyao Khamti's Failed Expedition Against the Chutias
summary: Nandi and Satyanarayana rule the Chutia kingdom from Sadhayapura (Sadiya), the earliest Chutia kings known from inscriptions. Tyao Khamti's campaign against them fails.
notes: Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive. The river withdrawal and opposing Chutia ruler are illustrative, not a documented personal confrontation; campaign dates vary.

name: Kamata and the Ahoms Drive Back Azam Shah
summary: The Kamata king, allied with Sudangphaa by marriage, drives Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah of Bengal back across the Karatoya. A Boko inscription shows the Sultanate held part of Kamrup for some years.
notes: Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive. Exact chronology and Ahom military participation are uncertain; the Sultan at the ford is an illustrative reconstruction. Sudangphaa is not shown in battle.

notes: Heritage University paper gives 1228–1265. Control over lands east of the Manas was loose. The reorganisation into the Kamata state is dated c. 1250–1270.
